- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after recent spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5), model often underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if price has recently dipped.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp upward moves (e.g., +5+ points in 1-2 days); apply a “cool-down” correction by reducing forecast by 10-20% of the spike magnitude.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., price drops after rising 3+ days), model often fails to recognize it; reduce forecast for next period if sentiment turns negative.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment shifts; use 7-day moving average of sentiment to smooth and adjust forecast bias.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– signals (e.g., +1, -1, +1), model often misaligns with true trend; favor the sentiment majority direction for 3-5 day horizon, then adjust for longer-term mean reversion.
